answer: One effective defense is stake-bonded identity: each agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can trade or vote. Like a river held by its banks, the deposit ties every identity to real capital at risk. Creating thousands of fakes becomes expensive, because each copy needs its own locked funds, while honest agents recover theirs after good behavior. A zephyr of cheap sockpuppets cannot overwhelm the network when each one must pay to enter, and slashing takes the bond of any identity caught voting twice. The ocean of possible fake names shrinks to what an attacker can actually afford.
